comments.text:
Used to join two sentences.
けれども (most formal) →けれど→けど (least formal)
けど used in speech, not when writing.
Using けれども etc to start a sentence is frowned upon. But, like using 'but' to start a sentence in English, is sometimes done anyway.
comments.html:
Used to join two sentences.
けれども (most formal) →けれど→けど (least formal)
けど used in speech, not when writing.
Using けれども etc to start a sentence is frowned upon. But, like using 'but' to start a sentence in English, is sometimes done anyway.

comments.text:
Verb, i-adjective or the copula should be before けれども.

e.g. 彼は１６歳だけれど、両親から独立しています。

comments.text:
In polite/formal use 
sentence-A [-masu] けれども sentence-B [-masu] can be used, but 
sentence-A [plain] けれど(も) sentence-B [-masu]
is also possible.

comments.text: I would like to express my displeasure in seeing wa/ha o/wo in Romaji. We are all supposed to know what they mean, so why write them as they don't sound? Why write "ha" when we all know it really sounds like "wa?" Why write "wo" when we know it really sounds like "o"? Why don't you write it like it sounds?
